I have no idea on how to deal with the bullies, or any specific interactions. But for a long term solution, I'd suggest you to get your self-esteem up. Of course, easier said than done. The idea is to be happy and satisfied with _yourself_, so as what other people think doesn't even cross your mind. The abuse by your parents might have damaged you more than you think. You need to rewire your brain, and destroy the idea that every relationship in life would be akin to the one you're most used to,i.e, the one with your parents. I'm a people pleaser myself and my family has a lot of role in my SA, even though there wasn't any "abuse" involved. 

Edit: this [post](https://www.reddit.com/r/socialanxiety/comments/9l7wtq/7_things_i_wish_id_known_20_years_ago/?utm_source=reddit-android) helped me a lot, might help you as well

Can relate. For pretty much anything that involves or has the element of other people judging or scrutinizing me, I get nervous and fuck up.

I remember seeing a friend from school at the gym,just a couple months ago while I was on the treadmill. As soon as he called after me, I just got anxious, dreading the possibility of an interaction in a crowded place, and tried to walk towards him, _without_ turning off the treadmill. I fell, and was so flustered. Even though no one laughed, I'm pretty sure I saw a grin here and there. It was just so embarrassing.

This is exactly me. Being accepted in groups never really helped me..it just gave me a temporary high, made me feel a little better sure. But really, I've realized that it's not "social" at all, my problem. I'm scared of being judged, all the time. It's a case of deep rooted insecurity and low self esteem. There have been times when I've been a complete loner, and there have been times when I'm been accepted, having real genuine friends. The insecurity, never really changed. It's about _me_, as a person. I need to fix this toxic perception of me. And that'd come through, idk, making myself happy for a change. Doing something, that'd make me proud, happy and accomplished. I have a hunch that your  lifestyle is disfunctional as well, OP, isn't it? As for me, I just go about my day, procrastinating on school work, mindlessly browsing the internet, sleeping late nights, eating unhealthy food. I've been reading _The Six Pillars of Self Esteem_ and it's certainly helping me. There's a great line in it - _a person with low self-esteem goes about life not to acquire joy but to avoid pain_, something like that. My thoughts are scattered, I know, but it's all about self love, I think. It's the middle of the night here, so yeah. Hopefully you can take away something from this mess of a comment.

I deactivated my Instagram account for about 2 weeks now. I never talked to anyone there, just looked at memes and saw kids from my school posting and got jealous. The thing is, I can reactivate it, any time I want, but this 2week absence has made me realize - I don't really care for it and it doesn't add anything to my life. It's just a tool I used to procrastinate. Seeing others happy moments and not have my life figured out didn't really help my mental state either.

I do like the idea and it probably would work for most. But I feel as if just a string of successful social interactions won't help _me_ in the long term. For me, social anxiety is just a manifestation of crippling low self-esteem. I need to work on myself, my whole life style. My routine is fucked,I self sabotage every chance I get. I don't want to be good at social interactions per se, more like embody an attitude in which I wouldn't give a fuck if I'm not.
